A uniform bar of mass $M$ and length $L$ has three notches along the bottom. The center notch is at the center of mass of the bar, and the other two notches are a distance of $\frac{L}{12}$ on either side of the center notch. The bar is placed on a fulcrum as shown. A mass $M$, equal to the mass of the bar itself, is hung a distance $\frac{L}{4}$ from the right edge of the bar. When an unknown mass $M'$ is hung a distance $\frac{L}{4}$ from the left edge of the bar, the system remains in static equilibrium. Calculate the unknown mass 
\[M'\] in terms of 
\[M\].

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal uniform long rod, with the total length marked as L. At the bottom of the long rod there are three adjacent notches, the central notch is near the center of the rod, and the distance between the left and right adjacent notches is marked as L/12. The triangular support point touches below the leftmost notch among the three notches. On the left side hangs an unknown mass M′, whose suspension point is L/4 from the left end; on the right side hangs mass M, whose suspension point is L/4 from the right end. Reasoning: Take the left end of the rod as x=0, and the right end as x=L. The center of gravity of the uniform rod is at x=L/2. Because the support point is at the notch L/12 to the left of the central notch, the support point position is x=L/2 - L/12 = 5L/12. The left-side mass M′ is at x=L/4 = 3L/12, so its lever arm to the support point is 5L/12 - 3L/12 = L/6, on the left side of the support point. The rod's own weight M g acts at x=L/2 = 6L/12, at a distance L/12 from the support point, on the right side of the support point. The right-side hanging mass M is at x=L - L/4 = 3L/4 = 9L/12, at a distance 9L/12 - 5L/12 = L/3 from the support point, on the right side of the support point. In static equilibrium, taking the support point as the pivot, the counterclockwise torque produced by the left-side M′ equals the clockwise torque produced by the rod's weight and the hanging mass M on the right side: M′ g (L/6) = M g (L/12) + M g (L/3). The right side combines to M g (L/12 + 4L/12) = M g (5L/12). Therefore M′/6 = 5M/12, solving gives M′ = 6·5M/12 = 2.5M.

method.method_draft: Use a direct torque balance about the fulcrum. First read from the image that the triangular fulcrum is under the left of the three bottom notches. From the text, the middle notch is at the bar center, and adjacent notches are L/12 apart, so the pivot is L/12 left of the bar center, at x = 5L/12 from the left end. The image/text place M' at L/4 from the left end and M at L/4 from the right end, i.e. x = L/4 and x = 3L/4. The uniform bar’s own weight M acts at x = L/2. Compute lever arms relative to the fulcrum: M' is L/6 to the left, the bar weight is L/12 to the right, and the hanging mass M is L/3 to the right. Set counterclockwise torque equal to clockwise torque: M'g(L/6) = Mg(L/12) + Mg(L/3). Solve to get M' = 2.5M.

图像描述：图中是一根水平的均匀长杆，标出总长度为 L。长杆底部有三个相邻的凹口，中央凹口在杆的中心附近，左右相邻凹口之间标为 L/12。三角形支点顶在三个凹口中最左边的凹口下方。左侧悬挂未知质量 M′，其悬挂点距左端为 L/4；右侧悬挂质量 M，其悬挂点距右端为 L/4。

In static equilibrium, taking the support point as the pivot, the counterclockwise torque produced by the left-side M′ equals the clockwise torque produced by the rod's weight and the hanging mass M on the right side: M′ g (L/6) = M g (L/12) + M g (L/3). The right side combines to M g (L/12 + 4L/12) = M g (5L/12). Therefore M′/6 = 5M/12, solving gives M′ = 6·5M/12 = 2.5M.

Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal uniform long rod, with the total length marked as L. At the bottom of the long rod there are three adjacent notches, the central notch is near the center of the rod, and the distance between the left and right adjacent notches is marked as L/12. The triangular support point touches below the leftmost notch among the three notches. On the left side hangs an unknown mass M′, whose suspension point is L/4 from the left end; on the right side hangs mass M, whose suspension point is L/4 from the right end.

Reasoning: Take the left end of the rod as x=0, and the right end as x=L. The center of gravity of the uniform rod is at x=L/2. Because the support point is at the notch L/12 to the left of the central notch, the support point position is x=L/2 - L/12 = 5L/12. The left-side mass M′ is at x=L/4 = 3L/12, so its lever arm to the support point is 5L/12 - 3L/12 = L/6, on the left side of the support point. The rod's own weight M g acts at x=L/2 = 6L/12, at a distance L/12 from the support point, on the right side of the support point. The right-side hanging mass M is at x=L - L/4 = 3L/4 = 9L/12, at a distance 9L/12 - 5L/12 = L/3 from the support point, on the right side of the support point. In static equilibrium, taking the support point as the pivot, the counterclockwise torque produced by the left-side M′ equals the clockwise torque produced by the rod's weight and the hanging mass M on the right side: M′ g (L/6) = M g (L/12) + M g (L/3). The right side combines to M g (L/12 + 4L/12) = M g (5L/12). Therefore M′/6 = 5M/12, solving gives M′ = 6·5M/12 = 2.5M.
